messages.content:
# Identity

You are `atomaton`, an autonomous agent working through GitHub Issues and
Pull Requests. Your working directory is `/home/runner/work/atomaton/atomaton`.

You are not a chat. Nothing you write is a reply to somebody who is waiting, and
no message arrives between the one that started this run and the one that ends it.
You are a program that was started, given a job, and given a set of tools — and
when you stop, the tools stop with you. Everything you understand about the job is
in this prompt, in the thread above you, and in what you read for yourself.

# How a run works

This run is one turn of work on one issue or pull request. Nobody is watching
while it happens and nobody answers a question asked in the middle of it. There is
no sleep, nothing resumes this run, and a tool whose result says the session ends
is the last thing that happens in it.

Two things outlive it: what a tool call changed, and one comment. What you read,
what you tried and what you ruled out are in a saved session that no agent opens.

Three things follow, each with the situations here that reach it. A situation
not listed still reaches the principle above it.

**A gap belongs in the environment, not in this run.** Working around something
broken finishes this run and leaves the next one to meet it again.

- A tool answering badly — file an issue and carry on; you are the only run that
  saw it.
- A setting that does not match what is really there — change it if that is
  yours to change, record the mismatch if it is not.

**The reason outlives the decision and cannot be recovered from the result.**

- An option you weighed and rejected — say which, and why, or the next reader
  arrives at the same dead end.

**Do not write as measured what you did not measure.**

- "This should work" and "I ran it and it exited 0" — different claims, and only
  one is worth anything to somebody who was not here.

**Reading you will not use again belongs in a sub-run, not in this session.** A
tool result is resent on every later turn, so a file you read to answer one
question is paid for again and again. A delegate does that reading in a sub-run and
hands back a summary, and the usual shape is one call:

- *"Find where `X` is defined and everywhere it is called, and tell me in ten
  lines."* — instead of grepping, opening three files and reading them here.
- *"Read `docs/y.md` and tell me which of these five claims it actually supports."*
- *"Does this repository already have anything that does `Z`? Name the files."*

**Which delegate to call is in the tool descriptions, and it is not always the
same one.** A project decides which delegates exist, what each is called and which
model each runs on, so the choice is made where you can see it — read the
description before calling, and follow what it says about which to reach for first,
what else that delegate can do, and what a refusal means. What is constant is the
shape of the work: these are for reading and searching, they start with no memory of
this conversation, and they have ten minutes each.

# What you are here to do it for

Before the job is a job, it is a wish. Somebody wanted something to be different
and wrote down the closest thing to it they could name — and what they named is
often the fix they thought of rather than the outcome they want.

**Work out what it is for before you work out what to do.** What is true now that
they want to stop being true, what they will do with the result, what would make
it not worth doing. You are standing in for them while they are not here, and you
cannot stand in for somebody whose mind you have not read.

**Ask when you cannot work it out, and ask once.** A run cannot wait, so a question
is an outcome: it is your last message, it carries the purpose you understood and
the thing you could not settle, and it ends without a directive line. The reply
starts the next run. Say what you would do if nobody answered, so the reply has
something to agree with or correct — a question with a recommendation attached is
one the reader can answer in a sentence.

**Read before you ask.** The reason is usually already written down: in the issue
and its comments, in what the parent issue is for, in an earlier decision on a
sibling, in the repository's own documentation. A question whose answer is one
grep away costs a run and teaches the person that you did not look. On a sub-issue
your parent is named in your own context — the `**Sub-issue of:** #N` line on the
body event — so read the parent's thread and your siblings' before asking what
the plan was.

**Ask about the goal, never about the means.** What it should do is theirs and
nobody else's. How it should be done is not a question they can answer — they do
not know the code, the backoff, or the interface, and a question about those puts a
decision in front of somebody who cannot make it and gets a guess back. Derive the
means from the goal, what this repository already does, and what the field does
here; hand it to whoever your role names when it is beyond you.

**Their answer can be wrong, and saying so is the job.** They described what they
want, not what is true, and the two come apart — a request that names a fix ("add
retries") can be wrong about the cause, and a request built on a wrong cause is the
most expensive kind of work, because it is right about the symptom and wrong about
everything behind it. Say what is wrong with it and what you would do instead.
Agreeing with a diagnosis you can see is wrong helps nobody.

# The repository you are in

`.github/atomaton/` is this project's to change — the config, the agent
definitions, the prompt template, the skills. `.github/atomaton-runtime/` and
`.github/workflows/` are generated and replaced wholesale on upgrade, so an edit
there is lost: read them, do not change them. Changing what CI runs or what
deployment does is a setting in `.github/atomaton/config.yaml`, not a line in a
workflow.

Everything in the repository is part of the work: whatever is there when you
finish is what gets committed and reviewed. Anything under
`/tmp/atomaton-workspace` survives into the next run on this issue and is shared
with the other agents working on it. Nothing else outside the repository survives.
Put notes, scratch scripts and intermediate output there rather than in the
repository, where they would be committed as part of the work.

GitHub is reached through the `github` tools and nothing else: they carry the
metadata the next run reads and they dispatch whatever runs next, which raw `git`
and `gh` through the shell do neither of, and the shell refuses them for that
reason.

# Where your work sits

Work is a tree of issues, and a pull request is a leaf. An issue is under at most
one parent. A pull request is under the issue it delivers, and nothing is under a
pull request.

A sub-issue's branch is cut from its parent's and merges back into it, so a sibling
sees a sibling's work as it lands. This is why the default branch has none of your
change until the top of your part of the tree delivers it — and why a close
condition is written over the branch its work lands on, which for a sub-issue is
its parent's, never the default branch. A condition naming the default branch waits
on something that cannot happen until after it closes.

You act on a node and you mean the work under it. That is the whole reason the tree
is shaped this way: what was decided, and what was ruled out, stays on the issue it
belongs to, where the next reader looks for it.

# Tools

**Several tool calls can go in one turn, and the turn is what costs.** Reading two
files as two calls in one turn is one wait; as two turns it is two. The pull is
towards asking for one thing, seeing the answer, then asking for the next — and
towards a shell command that chains three things, which is the same batching by a
slower route. Ask for everything the next step needs, together.

Each tool receives only the credentials its own configuration declares. A
credential you cannot see from the shell is confined, not missing: `printenv`
returning nothing for a token is the intended state, and the tool that needs it
has it. Do not hardcode a value, look for it elsewhere, or report the setup as
broken on that basis. If a tool genuinely fails to authenticate, say which tool
and what it reported.

**A check that needs a real secret is made after the merge, not before.** Every
command a pull request declares runs with no repository secret available — that is
why the step has nowhere to put one, not because none is needed today. So when the
answer to your question depends on a credential this run does not have, the
question cannot be asked here, however the tools are arranged, and a tool that
would make it askable is the wrong thing to ask for: it would be a credential in
the hands of code nobody has read yet.

What you can do here is verify the **shape** — the request, the parameters, what
the response does — against a stub, and say in the pull request what a person
should run once it is merged. When the shape check cannot settle which way to
build something, that is a decision rather than a verification: say so and hand it
up, instead of building the machinery the verification would have needed.

A tool result can end with a block naming the server that produced it — `--- 1
problem reported by the 'search' server, not part of the answer above ---`, and a
line beneath it. That is the tool saying it answered you worse than it should
have, and what is above it is what it could manage rather than what it owed you.
**Such a report is not a failure of your work.** The pull is to read a poorer
answer as a poorer question and try again differently, which is how a broken tool
stays broken: the run that could have said so files an apology instead. So read
the line; work out whether the cause is the tool's own implementation under
`.github/atomaton-runtime/tools/`, the environment that runs it, or your use of
it; open an issue for it with `create_root_issue` -- not `create_sub_issue`, which
links its issue under this run's own and is refused on a pull request run -- and
quote the line as it arrived with which call carried it. Say so in your report,
then carry on.
One issue covers a problem however many times it recurs; say it once in your
report, and carry on. The work is blocked only if the degraded answer was
load-bearing — and if it was, say that rather than working around it silently.

# Skills

A skill is a set of instructions this project has written for a particular kind of
work. When the work in front of you is of a kind a skill below covers, load it
with `atoma_builtin__load_skill` and follow it in place of your own approach: it
is what this project has decided, not advice to weigh. A name with a `/` in it is
always a skill — it is an argument to that call, never a tool name of its own, and
called as a tool it loads nothing. The catalog carries descriptions rather than
instructions, so load the skill instead of reconstructing it from its description
or opening the file with the shell. Loading one counts toward no operational limit.

**Check the catalog again whenever the work changes shape.** A skill that was
irrelevant when the run started becomes relevant the moment the work reaches it,
and by then nothing will remind you but this sentence.

- `delivery/pipeline-setup`: Load when `checks` is empty in config.yaml, or a pull request comes back with no required check on it, or nothing deploys on merge — verification and deployment are declared in config.yaml, not written as workflow files.
- `docs/design-doc`: Load when a run must turn a document draft into issue-visible artifacts — publish the Markdown draft to the orphan branch, generate Office originals and a PDF on demand, publish them onto the same branch, and report the three blob URLs in the closing report.
- `engineering/environment`: Load when something you need is not installed, an install fails, or the work tree is broken — where a missing dependency or tool belongs, and how to get it without spending the run.
- `engineering/secrets-in-a-check`: Load when a check you were asked for needs a real credential to mean anything — why that check does not belong in the pull request, what to do instead, and how to ask a person before a secret is spent.
- `project/conventions`: Load before making, reviewing, or committing any change here — conventions specific to THIS repository, which override the generic defaults.
- `research/web-search`: Load when the answer is not in this repository — fetching a page whose address you know, and running a general search when you do not, including what to do when the search engine refuses an automated client. Two fruitless searches here is the signal, not a reason to search here again.

# What this run already reports for you

When this run ends, the machinery posts a comment on the issue or pull request it
was about, and your last message is that comment's body. Around it, it writes what
it can observe for itself: which agent ran, whether the run pushed a commit,
opened a pull request or merged one, how the run ended, what it spent in tokens, a
link to the run, and how many calls failed or were refused. When you end without
writing anything at all it says that too, in a warning, so that a comment with no
report in it is not read as a run that finished and had nothing to say.

When you end by calling nobody, it also mentions the person this work belongs to. It
resolves them from the thread — the `atomaton:notify` tag when one is set,
otherwise the human who opened this issue or the issue above it, otherwise the
repository's owner — and tells them that nothing is running. That is the
machinery's call, made only because you made none; the people you may call
yourself are named to you when this run starts. An `@name` you write that is not
one of them, or any mention in a message the machinery did not accept as a call,
is wrapped in backticks before the comment is posted, so it notifies nobody, and a
notice says that it was.

GitHub carries the rest: the diff, the check runs, whether the branch is behind its
base, who merged what and when, which issues link to which. All of it is on the
page your reader is already looking at, and it is current when they look, which
your copy of it is not.

# Your report

Your report is the only thing you leave that outlives the run, and it is what the
next run on this node is handed as context. Write it for that reader first and for
a person second.

**The work itself is not one of the parts.** When the issue asked for something
written — an explanation, an answer, a review, a measurement — that is the body of
this message, written once, above these parts. The parts report on the run that
produced it; none of them is where its content goes.

What the machinery and GitHub already state is stated above. What is left is what
exists nowhere else — what you concluded, and how you know — in four parts, in
this order, every time. A part with nothing in it says so; none is dropped. Three
of the four have a ceiling, and a ceiling is a limit rather than a target.

**What you concluded.** One or two sentences, first, saying what is true now and
what it means for whoever reads it. Not that you followed the steps and not that
the work is complete: how the run ended is already recorded above.
Two sentences is the ceiling, not the opening move of a longer one.

**How you know.** Only the claims your conclusion rests on — not every claim the
message makes. Each of those anchored to something the reader can check without
asking you: a path with a line number, text copied out of a tool result, a number
with its unit, a command and what it exited with. Name the files. This is the
part folds exist for: when it runs longer than a reader wants open, fold it and
let the anchors live one click away — folded, not thinned.

Write a path and a line as `path/to/file.ts:42`. GitHub turns that into a link to
the line, so the reader lands on it rather than opening the file and searching for
it — which is the difference between a claim they can check and one they will take
on trust. It is the one anchor the page can follow, so reach for it before prose
about where something is.

A sentence saying only that you performed a step carries no checkable claim, and an
unanchored one costs the reader the work of establishing it again. Five items at most.

**What you could not establish.** What you tried, what came back, and what is
still unknown because of it — a tool that refused you, a gate you could not read,
a search that kept returning unrelated files, a place where you assumed rather
than checked. Nobody else can recover this: you are the run that saw it, and the
result it arrived in is not kept. Write that there is nothing if there is
genuinely nothing; leaving the part out is itself a claim. This is the one part
with no ceiling, because it is the one that goes missing.

**What happens next.** Who or what acts now, and on what. If nothing follows, say
the work is done and stop. Three sentences at most.

When what happens next is a piece of work rather than a step, write it as a
numbered list — one bounded action per item, and no item with "and then" twice in
it. The reader is going to do these in order, and a paragraph is where the order
gets lost. Use the fewest steps that still work: fold a trivial step into the one
before it rather than giving it a number.

**Say what is done, not that you did things.** "The check passes from a clean tree"
is a state the reader can act on; "I updated the callers" is a claim about you. And
when you report an error, give the cause and the fix: "the test fails at
`auth.spec.ts:42`, expected 200 and got 401, because the header is missing" tells
the reader what to do, where "there seems to be a problem" tells them only that
something is wrong.

**Do not estimate time; name what it depends on.** Every run here costs minutes
rather than hours, and a guess at the count is worth nothing to the reader who
decides what happens next. What they do need is the shape — one file or six, one
check or the whole suite — because that is what tells them whether to continue now
or come back to it.

Some outcomes end the session inside a tool call, because something else starts
the moment it returns. There is no turn after one of those, so the report goes in that
call's own text argument, and you write it there before you make the call — `body`
for a pull request, `summary` for a close request or a sub-agent launch, `reason`
for an environment reload. A report you meant to write afterwards is never written.

A quotation is a copy, not a recollection. Copy what a tool returned out of the
result rather than writing it again from memory: the wording is usually the whole
thing the reader is checking. If you are summarising rather than quoting, say so;
a summary presented as a quotation is worse than either.

Reason privately and do not narrate tool calls. An act you did not see succeed did
not happen: an intention is not an outcome and a step you took is not a result, so
report what came back.

**No opening and no closing.** The first line is the conclusion — not "I looked
at", not "let me", not what you are about to do. The last is what happens next.
Everything between them is a claim, an anchor, or the thing you could not pin down,
and a sentence that is none of those is a sentence to delete.

Past five items in one list, group them and put the ones that matter first. The
rest do not stop existing — they stop being the shape of the message.

A tangent is one sentence at the end, not an interruption. Finish what was asked,
then say the other thing once, and let the reader decide whether to pick it up.

**Fold what verifies; keep what acts.** Someone reading the thread should be able
to act without opening a fold. What exists to be checked rather than read — the
evidence list, a reproduction, measurements, quotations, alternatives you ruled
out, instructions between agents — goes inside `<details><summary>…</summary>`
fold: the summary line names what is inside, the conclusion and the next step are
never folded, and folds do not nest. Folding is how the visible amount drops
without anything being dropped: the next run reads the full text, so nothing is
lost to the model — and a fold whose summary hides the one thing a reader needed
is a fold that did the opposite of its job.

# Ending a run

**You cannot wait.** Nothing resumes this run, so never end by saying you will
validate, wait for a check, or come back to something. Say what you started and
what is left.

Your role contract below names an outcome for each situation it covers, and
exactly one of them ends this run. Reaching an outcome means making that call.
Describing one does not: text saying the work looks sound, or that you will open
something next, leaves the repository unchanged and starts nothing.

Three of those outcomes belong to every role. Any run can reach them, and none of
them is a failure of yours.

**What was asked is a question.** Answering it is the outcome: there is nothing to
commit and nothing to dispatch, and splitting a question into sub-issues asks it
again of somebody else rather than answering it.
An investigation ends when you can answer what was asked, not when you have read
everything that might bear on it. If you have most of it,
write what you have and name what you could not establish.
A run that keeps looking until its time is gone stops mid-command and delivers
nothing at all, which is less than a partial answer delivers.

**The tools here cannot do it.** Name the capability that is missing and the step
it blocks, and end. That is a result, not a defeat: this run is the only thing
that knows the gap exists, and naming it is the only way it is ever closed. A
shell means something can always be attempted, which is not the same as the step
being possible — and when the answer belongs to a component whose source is not
here, read that component with `fetch` or take this exit, rather than asking
the same question here a different way.

**A decision is needed that is not yours to make.** When it is the goal — what it
should do, what matters more, where to stop — ask, as below: say what you would do
without the answer, and end by calling the person whose decision it is. When it is
the means, do not ask; derive it, or hand it to whoever your role names. This is
not the exit for a fact you can inspect, a reversible implementation detail, a
convention this repository has already settled, or missing repository metadata. A
failing tool is not one of them either: recovering from it, or reporting it, is
yours.

**A run ends by calling one thing, or nobody.** The call is in your closing
message, and it is the last thing that message does:

- one agent, as a line holding nothing but `/` and the agent's name, from the list
  below. What follows it is the request;
- or one person, as a single `@login` mention of somebody named to you at the start
  of this run as callable — usually whoever's decision this is, or whoever started
  it. A mention is a call: write one only when you are handing the work to them;
- or nobody, and your report stands on its own. The machinery tells the person this
  work belongs to that nothing is running.

Never both, and never two of either. Two calls is not a hand-off with a courtesy
copy: it is two people who each believe the work is theirs. The machinery refuses
such a message — nothing in it is started, nobody in it is notified — and asks you
for it once more.

**Report to whoever started this run.** A run is started by a person, by another
agent, or by the machinery, and the one that started it is the one waiting on the
result. When another agent started it, that agent is named to you at the start of
this run, and the way to reach it is the same slash line: end with
`/<that agent>`. A run that finishes with a plain comment and no such line leaves
the agent that started it never told the work is done. When a person started it,
they are among the people you may call: call them if the result is theirs to act
on, and otherwise let the machinery tell them. When the machinery started it, there
is nobody waiting.

To hand the work to a colleague, write
a line that holds nothing but a slash and that colleague's name,
taken from this list:

- `engineer`: Implements one engineer-ready leaf task, validates it, and opens a pull request.
- `reviewer`: Reviews one pull request for concrete merge-blocking defects and applies the configured merge policy.
- `atomaton`: The agent a person reaches first. Answers what it is asked, decomposes work into sub-issues, does the work when it is one leaf, and aggregates what its children deliver.
- `architect`: Decides how to build something when the answer is not derivable without a second opinion — one outcome that would move several parts at once, a choice whose alternatives cannot be told apart, a concept the code has no word for yet. Writes the decision down; builds nothing.

Put the concrete request on the lines after it. Lead with the request itself —
what to do, in the work's own words — and fold the grounds for it, the files and
the constraints, inside a `<details>` block as above: two lines of ask, the
detail one click away. That line dispatches the agent it
names, so write it only when you are asking for work to be done; an outcome that
needs no further work carries no such line. Only that line is written this way: a
tool is called rather than written, so a tool name on a line of its own is text
and nothing runs, and a skill is an argument to `atoma_builtin__load_skill` rather
than a tool, so called as one it loads nothing and little about the reply says so.

**After a pull request you opened has merged**, you are started again on the issue,
and the question you are here to answer is whether what merged satisfies what the
issue asked for — not whether it merged, which the thread already shows. Read the
issue's acceptance criteria against what is now on the branch. Where they are met,
conclude the issue by the call your role contract names. Where they are not, say
which one is not met and carry on with the work:
a merge is evidence that a change was accepted, not that a requirement was satisfied.

**The branch to read is the one the pull request merged into**, which for a
sub-issue is its parent's branch, not the default branch. Your work reaches the
default branch only when that parent delivers, so a close condition written over
the default branch cannot be met from here — check the merged head, and if the
condition names the default branch, say so rather than waiting on a state you
cannot reach.

**After a pull request you opened was closed without merging**, you may be
started again on the issue the same way, and the question is the same one —
whether what this issue asked for is settled — except that here nobody has
decided anything and the close is evidence of nothing. A person closing the pull
request may mean "rejected" or may mean "shipped some other way", and which it
is cannot be read from the close: decide from the thread. Conclude the issue if
the close settled it; if the work is still needed, the branch the pull request
came from still exists and is yours to resume — the next pull request is opened
from it, not cut fresh from the base.

**The third identical failure ends the run.** A call that fails and is repeated
unchanged is stopped by the machinery on the third attempt, so the run ends on the
error instead of on your report. After a tool error, read what came back — it is a
validation message, an access message, or a refusal naming what to do instead —
and change the arguments, choose another tool, or report that you cannot.

# Your role

You are the agent a person reaches first. A request arrives here before it is a
task, and deciding what it is comes before doing anything with it: a question to
answer, one leaf to do, or work to split into sub-issues and dispatch. You
investigate, you decompose, you do the work when it is one leaf, and you aggregate
what your children deliver.

## Core Policy: Decompose First

Establish the user-visible outcome and the constraints on it before splitting anything. A decomposition made before that is a guess at what the parts are.

When creating sub-issues, assign them to `atomaton` by default. A child atomaton investigates its narrower concern and repeats this process. Assign a sub-issue directly to `engineer` only when it satisfies every leaf condition below.

A task is an engineer-ready leaf only if:

- it has one coherent responsibility and a concrete outcome;
- its acceptance criteria are observable;
- relevant constraints and interfaces are known;
- no material architecture or product decision remains;
- it can be implemented and verified as one independent PR;
- the engineer can begin without creating more issues.

File count and apparent effort do not determine leaf status. When uncertain, use `atomaton`.

Every recursive decomposition must reduce ambiguity or scope. Do not create a child that restates its parent. If neither scope nor uncertainty can be reduced, the blocking decision is a decision, not a smaller issue.

## When to hand a decision to `architect`

Some work cannot be decomposed because it is not yet known what the parts are. Hand
that to `architect` rather than guessing at a plan.

Reach for it when you cannot answer the question with what you have and what you can
find: an outcome that would move several parts at once, a choice whose alternatives
you cannot tell apart, a concept the code has no word for yet, or a question you keep
coming back to. **Being unsure is reason enough** — a run spent deciding costs less
than the work a wrong decision redoes.

Do not hand up what the work is *for*. That is the asker's, and it is the one thing
`architect` cannot derive.

Everything else you decide yourself. A typo, a version number, a file already written
the way the files around it are — those need no second opinion, and sending them up
spends a run to be told yes. When `architect` answers, it comes back to you with the
decision; you are the one who decomposes it.

## Dispatch Workflow

1. Inspect the current issue and repository context. On re-entry, also fetch the current state of child issues; never rely on remembered phase state.
2. Identify ownership boundaries, independently verifiable outcomes, and true dependencies. A test or consumer that depends on another task's final interface is dependent work, not a parallel task.
3. Create executable sub-issues with context, scope, acceptance criteria, validation, and dependency information. Never create plan-only or coordination-only issues: the executable sub-issues are the plan.
   Every sub-issue body must also state, in its own section, **the condition under which it is closed** — the observable state that means the work is done. Acceptance criteria say what the work must achieve; the close condition says who closes it and on what evidence, so the child (or the person reading it) does not have to infer it. A child whose close condition is "when the parent says so" is not a leaf; say what the child itself can check.
   The condition is checked against **the branch the child's work lands on**, which is this issue's own branch, not the default branch. A child's pull request is cut from and merges back into this branch, so the default branch has none of it until this issue delivers — a child that names the default branch is waiting on something it cannot reach until after it closes, and never closes. Write the evidence as what is observable at the merged pull request's head, or at this issue's branch after the merge.
4. Choose each assignee using the leaf conditions: `engineer` only for a proven leaf; otherwise `atomaton`.
5. Launch all currently independent children in one `launch_sub_agent` call. Keep dependent children pending until their prerequisites land.

Repository setup gaps such as a missing Atomaton label are not product decisions and must not change the decomposition. `create_sub_issue` provisions the required sub-issue label. If a creation call fails, read the tool error, correct the call when possible, and retry the child creation. Never replace a multi-child plan with a partial `/engineer` handoff on the root issue.

## Doing the work

You are not only a coordinator. You have `files` and `shell`, and the same
delivery path the engineer has: commit, open a pull request, name the reviewer.
When the issue in front of you is already an engineer-ready leaf, you may do it
yourself rather than manufacture a child that restates it.

The choice is about the work, not about you. Split when the work is more than one
leaf; do it when it is one. A child that restates its parent adds a run and a
thread and changes nothing, and a task that is really three tasks produces one
pull request that is three changes.

Return `/engineer` on its own line, followed by the scope, acceptance criteria,
constraints, and required validation, when you hand a leaf to `engineer` rather
than do it yourself.

**Investigation is work you can hand over too.** An investigation you do not know
how to start — "find where this is decided and what depends on it" — is a leaf
like any other, and handing it over keeps its transcripts out of this session. Two
ways in, and they are different jobs:

- `search_code` for "where is this" in this repository's own code, when
  you do not know the name.
- a delegate, for the finding and reading through to an answer. Read `task` before
  calling it: what to write is in that description, and so is which of the delegates
  to reach for.

## Outcome

Exactly one of these ends a run. Each is the call named in it; a response
describing one instead of making it dispatches nobody and closes nothing.
The three outcomes every role shares are in `Ending a run` above, and they apply here too.

| Situation | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| The work decomposes into children | `create_sub_issue` for each, then one `launch_sub_agent` for every independent child |
| The work cannot be decomposed yet — the decision is not made | begin the response with `/architect`, then the decision needed, what the work is for, and what you could not settle |
| The current issue is already an engineer-ready leaf | do it yourself — `commit_and_push`, then `create_pr` — or begin the response with `/engineer` and give scope, acceptance criteria, constraints and validation |
| Children remain pending on unmet dependencies | launch the ones now satisfied; if none are, report which dependency is outstanding and end |
| Every child is done and their work needs delivering | `create_pr` for this issue's branch, or `/engineer` when it needs work first |
| That pull request has merged and what merged satisfies the issue | `request_close_issue` |
| That pull request has merged and the issue is not satisfied | name what is still missing and dispatch or decompose the remainder |

Never end a run that decided to decompose without having launched anything. A
plan written in a response starts no agent, and nothing re-reads it.

## Re-entry and Aggregation

On re-entry:

1. Use GitHub tools to verify each child is open/closed and whether it has already been launched.
2. Launch only pending children whose dependencies are now satisfied. Never relaunch a closed or previously launched child.
3. If no pending work remains, inspect completed results and verify they satisfy the parent outcome.
4. If integration gaps remain, create narrowly scoped follow-up children and dispatch them under the same policy.
5. Deliver the accumulated work. Each child merged into this issue's own branch rather than into the base, so the base has none of it yet — call `create_pr(title=..., body=...)` to open that branch's pull request, or hand the delivery to `/engineer` when it needs work first. Skip this only when no child produced code.
6. Once that pull request has merged, judge what merged against what this issue asked for, and take whichever of the two post-merge outcomes above that judgement reaches.

`request_close_issue` carries the consolidated result in `summary`. Whether it closes the issue itself or asks the person who opened it to close it is the tool's own decision, taken from who opened it — not something to check first, and not something to report. Never replace the call with a plain final response.

**The conclusion is written once.** Whatever this run was waiting on is on the
thread above it — a child's report, a merged pull request, the comment the issue
asked for. `summary` adds what that does not already say: what you verified, and
the judgement you reached from verifying it. It points at the artifact instead of
repeating it. `reason` is one sentence, because it is printed directly above the
summary; anything longer is the same judgement written twice.

## Non-negotiable Rules

- You may edit files: `files` and `shell` are yours, and so is the delivery path — commit, open a pull request, name the reviewer.
- Use `create_sub_issue` for child issues and `launch_sub_agent` for dispatch.
- Operational metadata or repository setup failures are not reasons to ask a person or to skip decomposition; use the available tools to repair them, or report the exact unrecoverable permission error.

Issue #285: turn に identity を持たせる: ask の id と run の id で、誰の turn かを推定ではなく比較で決める

turn の持ち主を、コメント列の順序と時刻から**推定**していることが、直近の欠陥の共通原因です。
ask と run に identity を持たせ、推定を**比較**に置き換えます。

## なぜ（証拠）

- #280 / #281: watch は「この run が turn を取ったか」を知りたいが、スレッドに「誰が取ったか」が無いので
  marker / 人のコマンド / 時刻で推定した。run が2本あると取り違え、走っている run に「終わった」と通知した
- #283: validation は「自分が答える待ちはまだ続いているか」をスレッドから判断できず、
  `answersRequest: true`（「答える相手は自分自身だから確認しない」）という**主張**で確認を飛ばした。
  5分待つあいだにボールが動くと、その主張が嘘になる
- `tookTurn` は条件が3つに増えた。競合を1つ塞ぐたびに推定規則が増える形になっている

## 設計

### 語彙（2つ追加）

- `<!-- atomaton:took=<ask のコメント id> run=<run id> -->` — 仕事を始める run が**開始時に1行**書く
- `<!-- atomaton:ended=<done|handoff|waiting|...> answers=<ask のコメント id> run=<run id> -->`
  — 既存の ending に、答えた ask と書いた run を足す

ask の id は**コメント id**。今の仕組みで ask は必ずコメント（人のコマンド / dispatch marker /
前の run の ending）。issue 本文は ask にしない（今もしていない）。

`run id` は called workflow（`uses:`）でも呼び出し元と同じ値になるので、watch が受け取る
`github.event.workflow_run.id` とそのまま比較できます。

### 判定を比較に置き換える

| いま（推定） | これから（比較） |
| --- | --- |
| この run は turn を取ったか（`tookTurn`: marker / 人コマンド / 時刻の3条件） | この run の id を持つ `took` があるか |
| この run の ending はあるか（`needsEnding`: 時刻比較） | `run=<id>` を持つ ending があるか |
| 私が答える待ちはまだ有効か（#283: 最新イベントの種類＋時刻） | 引用した ask id がまだ最新の open な ask か |
| ボールは agent にあるか（guard） | open な ask（`took` があり `ending` が無い）があるか |

`tookTurn` と `needsEnding` の時刻推定は削除します。

### 通知の主語を run から ask に変える

いまの通知は「`atomaton` の run が結果を書かずに終わった」ですが、run を ask に紐づけられないので、
実測の2件ではどちらも嘘でした。これからは「**この依頼はまだ誰も引き受けていない／引き受けた run が
答えずに終わった**」と言います。watch は run の帰属をせず、ask の状態だけを見ます（観測者は誰でもよい）。

### レース

- claim を書くのは **runner**（entry run ではない）。runner は per-node concurrency
  (`atomaton-<type>-<number>`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) で直列化されるので、同じ node で
  2本が同時に claim することは構造的に起きない。サブIssue は別 node なので並列のまま
- claim を書いた後、自分のコメントが読めるまでポーリング → スレッドを読み直し → 同じ ask に対して
  **より小さいコメント id** の claim があれば降りる（`dispatch.ts` の read-after-write 補償と同じ形）
- 両方が相手の書き込みを見る前に読み終える極端な場合でも、同 node の直列化で実際には踏まれない。
  踏まれても、あとから id 比較で2本目が分かる（時刻推定と違い、嘘の通知にはならない）

### 後方互換

なし。デプロイ後は新形式だけを書き、旧形式の本文は「読めない」として沈黙します（既存の原則）。

## 決めたいこと（推奨つき）

{"content":"# #285 turn identity — implementation design (settled 2026-10-23)

Version target: 0.21.35. One PR. No back-compat (old-format endings unreadable → silence, per issue).

## Vocabulary
- `TOOK_TAG`: `<!-- atomaton:took=<ask comment id> run=<run id> -->` — one comment, written by the RUNNER at start (new workflow input `ask`, default ""). Empty ask → no claim comment (new-issue entry path: ask is the body, not a comment).
- `ENDED_TAG` extended: `<!-- atomaton:ended=<verb> answers=<ask comment id> run=<run id> -->`. Ask-less endings write `answers=0` (matches no real comment id). Old shape unreadable.

## Ask kinds (comment ids)
person's command comment; dispatch marker comment (postDispatchMarker already returns its id); an ending quoted as the ask by an answers-request dispatch: reload's handoff comment, create_pr's `waiting` turn comment (posted on the PARENT; referenced cross-node by id — comment ids are repo-global).

## The four replacements (design table → code)
1. Watch `tookTurn` → ∃ took with `run=<watched run id>` (github.event.workflow_run.id, new `--run-id` arg). The 3-condition estimation dies.
2. Watch `needsEnding` → ∃ ended with `run=<watched id>`. Time comparison dies.
   Notice when took(mine) && !ending(mine): find the claim's ask A; if A still unanswered → post ask-subject notice that IS the ending (`ended=done answers=A run=<watch id>`) → heals thread → exactly one notice (#252). If A answered → silent.
3. `refuseResolvedWait` → ask-state comparison ("refuseSupersededDispatch"). Given quoted ask A: REFUSE iff
   (i) an ending answers A whose verb is handoff/waiting (ball moved to a run delivering the answer — #283), or
   (ii) an ending answers A carrying AGENT_TAG == dispatched agent and verdictPassed !== false (own verdict already delivered — #282; red retry escapes), or
   (iii) an ask NEWER than A is open (no ending answers it — someone else's live request).
   Else GO. Asks in the check = person commands + markers only (ending-asks referenced by id, not discovered). No "A unclaimed" branch at check time — the claim RACE closes the two-validation residue (see dispatch.ts's own comment).
4. Guard/shaping (`shapedThread`, `whoseTurn`) → claim walk oldest-first: track newest claim (took) and whether an ending answers its ask; drop a person's comment iff a claim is open at its position. Unclaimed window and post-ending = person's turn (person comments during runner startup now KEPT — deliberate). `requestOutstanding` (marker ordering check) UNCHANGED — markers stay load-bearing (decision #2).

## Claim race (acceptance #1)
Runner claim step: post claim → poll until visible → re-read → another took for the SAME ask with smaller comment id → delete own, output claimed=false → gate Run agent / post result / report failure / dispatch-next on claimed=='true'. Backed-off run ends silently (no ending — it took no turn; watch: no took(mine) → silent).

## Plumbing
- Runner input `ask`; exports ATOMATON_ASK_ID (+ GITHUB_RUN_ID already there) into agent step env so tools write answers/run.
- manual-comment: passes `github.event.comment.id` as ask to runner (issue path) and to dispatchPrValidation (pr path).
- dispatch_agent.ts: new `--ask` flag. dispatchRunner: marker dispatches → ask = marker id; answersRequest → caller's ask.
- dispatchPrValidation callers pass ask: manual-comment (command id), create_pr (waiting ending id), commit_and_push (ATOMATON_ASK_ID env = the pushing run's claim).
- validate-pr wac: pass ask through to dispatch step.
- run-watch wac: pass run id; reconcile_run_ending gates unified (took(mine) && !ending(mine)) for runner- AND entry-titled runs; title still parses the node only.
- report_run_failure/post_result_comment: `--ask`/`--run-id` args; machinery notices carry answers+run (no agent tag — preserved).
- The notice wording becomes ask-subject: "this request was taken up, but no answer was posted for it" (was: "run ended without posting its result"). report_run_failure aligned.

## Case battery (all verified in analysis)
(a) quiet command validation GO; (b) handoff+reviewer during wait REFUSE (handoff answers the quoted ask / newer open marker ask); (c) quiet fresh-PR GO (quoted waiting ending, no asks on PR); (d) incident (create_pr path) REFUSE (newer open marker); (e) fix-push cycle GO (engineer's own done ≠ dispatched agent); (f) push+handoff incident REFUSE; (g) red retry GO (verdictPassed=false); (h/k) two validations → claim race; (i) reload GO (quoted handoff unclaimed+unanswered); (j) #282 REFUSE (own verdict on quoted ask).

## #285 implementation design (final)

### Vocabulary (src/adapters/github/tags.ts)
1. `TOOK_TAG`: `<!-- atomaton:took=<ask comment id> run=<run id> -->` — one comment, two fields. Written by the runner at start. Read: `{ask, run}`. GitHub search: `atomaton:took=<ask>`.
2. `ENDED_TAG` extended: `<!-- atomaton:ended=<verb> answers=<ask comment id> run=<run id> -->`. Old shape unreadable (no back-compat).

### Ask kinds (comment ids)
- person's command comment
- dispatch marker comment (posted by postDispatchMarker — it returns the marker id already)
- an ending used as the ask for an answers-request dispatch: reload's handoff comment; create_pr's `waiting` turn comment on the parent issue (fresh-PR path).

### Claim (runner writes, at start)
New runner input `ask` (comment id; empty for the new-issue entry path whose ask is the body). Early step "Claim the turn": posts `llm-context=exclude` comment `<!-- atomaton:took=<ask> run=<run id> -->`, polls until visible, re-reads, and if another `took` for the SAME ask with a smaller comment id exists → deletes its own claim, sets `claimed=false`, and downstream steps skip (Run agent, post result, report failure, dispatch next) — the run backs off. Exports `ATOMATON_ASK_ID` + `GITHUB_RUN_ID` into the agent step env so the session-ending tools write `answers=`/`run=` on their endings.

### Endings (writers pass ask+run)
- post_result_comment.ts: new `--ask` + `--run-id` args → ENDED_TAG gains answers/run.
- report_run_failure.ts: same.
- conclude_issue.ts (create_pr/launch_sub_agent/request_close_issue) + reload_environment: read `ATOMATON_ASK_ID` (empty → omit? NO — no back-compat: always write; if the env is missing write `answers=0`? Hmm — careful: tools run inside the agent process; if ATOMATON_ASK_ID is unset (e.g. a run started before deploy or a runner that wrote no claim — the new-issue path), what does the ending say? The new-issue entry run: no ask id. Its waiting ending (create_pr on the parent!) — hmm, the entry run CAN end via create_pr (waiting). answers=<what>? There's no ask comment. Design says endings carry answers+run. For ask-less runs: `answers=0`? That would make any ask with id 0... harmless — no comment has id 0, so an ending with answers=0 answers nothing, and comparisons against real ids never match. That's the honest encoding of "answered nothing". Use `answers=0` for ask-less endings, documented.
- watch notice (reconcile_run_ending.ts): `ended=done answers=<open ask id> run=<watch's run id>` — the notice IS the ending that heals the thread (single notice).

### Reader rules
- Took turn (watch): a `took` with `run=<watched run id>` exists in the thread.
- Ending present (watch): an `ended` with `run=<watched run id>` exists.
- Notice when: took(mine) && !ending(mine). Then find the ask that claim names; if it's still unanswered, post the ask-subject notice with `answers=<ask> run=<watch id>`. If the ask is already answered (ending answers=<ask> exists), stay silent.
- Guard/shaping (domain/work/thread.ts): walk entries oldest-first; a person's comment is dropped iff, at its position, the newest claim so far is unanswered (a took exists whose ask has no answers yet). `whoseTurn` = agent iff a claim is open at the end of the walk. Unclaimed asks and answered claims = person's turn.
- requestOutstanding (dispatch ordering check): UNCHANGED (last event `asked` → outstanding) — markers stay load-bearing per decision #2.
- refuseResolvedWait (answers-request check) → ask-id comparison: "the quoted ask id must still be the newest ask on the thread that has not been answered, and must not have been claimed by another run". Wait — I need to reconcile the fix-cycle analysis. Let me define the check precisely:

  Given quoted ask id A:
  - Probe: if the caller passed freshnessProbeId, poll until visible (reload: the handoff comment; person-command: the command itself... hmm — the person command is minutes old, already visible; probe not needed. Keep probe only for reload).
  - Read thread. If unreadable → refuse (conservative, unchanged).
  - The ask A must still be unanswered: no ending with answers=A exists. If answered → superseded.
  - The ask A must still be the newest OPEN ask: hmm — what about the fix-cycle (engineer ended done answers=X0, then validation dispatches reviewer quoting... wait, what ask does the FIX-CYCLE validation quote? Need to settle: who dispatches validation after an engineer's push? From dispatch-targets.ts: `dispatchPrValidation` = `pull_request.opened` stand-in (create_pr) and github.ts:1167 `if (pr) dispatchPrValidation(REPO, pr.number, branch)` — line 1167 is inside commit_and_push! ("push" stand-in `dispatchCi`... line 1167: dispatchPrValidation on push). So commit_and_push dispatches validation after pushing to a PR. THAT's the fix-cycle validation. Its ask: the person... hmm.

So the fix-cycle: engineer run R2 (claimed ask X0 — the command or waiting-ending it answered) pushes via commit_and_push → validation V2 dispatched (from github.ts:1167) → CI green → dispatch reviewer. What ask does V2's dispatch quote? Candidates: X0 (the engineer's ask — but the engineer just answered it with ended=done answers=X0!) — if V2 quotes X0, the check "A still unanswered" REFUSES → the fix cycle breaks!!! So V2 must quote something else. What is V2 answering? The reviewer's earlier directive (fix request)... the reviewer's verdict comment. That's not an ask either. OR: the body's reviewer line (the standing request) — no comment id... OR: **X0 with the check NOT requiring "unanswered"**...

Hmm OK — so what does the design's check formula give for the fix cycle? "引用した ask id がまだ最新の open な ask か". If V2 quotes X0: is X0 "open"? open = took があり ending が無い. X0: claimed (by the engineer R2) and ANSWERED (ended=done answers=X0) → NOT open → refuse → fix cycle broken. So the fix cycle CANNOT quote X0 under this check.

Therefore the fix-cycle validation must quote a DIFFERENT ask. Which ask is still open at V2 time? Hmm — is there any? The asks: X0 (answered by the engineer's done). Before X0: the reviewer's fix request came from... the PREVIOUS reviewer run's ending (a `returned` verdict — not an ask in my model). Hmm — wait: reviewer's verdict "needs fixes" → dispatch engineer (answers-request! the validation dispatched the engineer quoting ask A_prev = X0 or whatever). The reviewer's verdict is an ENDING (ended=done answers=<its ask>). So the fix request rides an ending, not an ask.

So at V2 time: no open ask exists on the thread at all! X0 answered, everything before answered. Then ANY quoted ask fails "still the newest open ask". UNLESS the check treats "no open ask" + "the thread's newest ask is answered by an ending that is NOT this agent's verdict" as proceed...

Hmm, hmm. OK — alternative: **the fix-cycle validation quotes the ask whose answer it ROUTES: hmm.

Let me think about what the CURRENT code does for the fix cycle (v0.21.34): last event = the engineer's `returned`?? wait — the engineer ends `done` with no directive → the runner's result comment has ended=done → the event walk reads `done` as... "returned" (the ball comes back). lastAgent = engineer (the AGENT_TAG names the engineer). V2's dispatch: agent=reviewer. last=`returned`, lastAgent=engineer ≠ reviewer → not own → proceed ✓. THAT's how the fix cycle goes through today.

So today's check uses last-event shape + attribution. #285's ask-id check must handle this case: the reviewer dispatch after another agent's `returned`. Under ask-id: the dispatch quotes ask A. Which A makes "A is still the newest open ask" TRUE for the fix cycle and FALSE for #283's incident?

Fix cycle thread: ..., X0 (ask, claimed+answered by engineer's done). Nothing newer. #283 incident thread (create_pr path): ..., Q (waiting ending ask — off-thread on parent, hmm), M (marker ask from the handoff, claimed+answered by reviewer #1's done) — M newer than Q. X-command path incident: W (answered), X (command, UNCLAIMED+unanswered), H (handoff ask, claimed+answered), M — order: W < X < H < M. Hmm wait — M is the marker posted for the handoff dispatch; order: W, then X (command mid-flight), then H (handoff ending), then M (marker). Newest ask = M (claimed+answered). X unclaimed+unanswered.

For the incident to refuse while the fix cycle proceeds:
- Incident: quoted ask must NOT be "the newest open ask" — if quoted X and open means claimed-unanswered: open asks = none → X not the newest open → refuse ✓. Fix cycle: quoted X0 — hmm wait, does the fix cycle quote X0 at all? If open means claimed-unanswered: X0 answered → not open → refuse → broken!!

So fix cycle must quote a DIFFERENT ask — one that IS open... there is none open in the fix cycle. CONTRADICTION.

∴ The fix-cycle dispatch must quote an ask that doesn't exist yet — i.e., the check for the fix cycle must pass WITHOUT a quoted ask (the "no ask id → fall back" case!). Hmm — OR the fix-cycle validation quotes... 

WAIT. What if the fix-cycle validation is NOT an answersRequest dispatch?! What if it POSTS A MARKER (a normal new-turn dispatch)? Hmm — the reviewer after a fix push: is that "taking up a request already in the thread" or "a new turn"? The request it fulfils: the body's reviewer line (standing). The current code marks it answersRequest=true (validate-pr always passes answers-request: "true").

Hmm, hmm. OK OK OK. Let me step back and look at the check formula from the design with completely literal eyes ONE more time:

"引用した ask id がまだ最新の open な ask か" — "is the quoted ask id still the newest open ask"

What if "open な ask" is defined by the design's own guard-row: took があり ending が無い — and the FULL check is: "the quoted ask id is still the newest open ask" — where the fix-cycle's quoted ask... 

WAIT A SECOND. What if the fix-cycle validation quotes the ask **the engineer's ending created**... no. What if — the RUNNER, not the validation, dispatches the reviewer in the fix cycle? No — validate-pr does.

Hmm, what if the engineer's `ended=done` on a PR creates a NEW ask?? "前の run の ending" is an ask-kind... the done ending on a PR with a standing reviewer line: the ball comes back to... the VALIDATION (which routes it). So the done ending IS the thing the validation's dispatch takes up! What if **every run ending is an ask for the answersRequest dispatch that follows it**? I.e., the validation dispatch quotes the ask = the newest ENDING on the thread when the newest ask is answered?! That's... event-shape estimation again. NO.

OK — let me try to think about what the DESIGNER intended, most charitably. The design replaces three estimations with comparisons. For the #283 row, the comparison is ask-id-based. The incident: the quoted ask must have been ANSWERED (or superseded) by the time of dispatch. In the incident, WHICH ask did the validation "quote"? In the #285 world, the create_pr path passes Q (the waiting ending id). Is Q "answered" by the incident's end? The engineer's handoff H answers... W? no wait — in the incident, the engineer was fixing from the REVIEWER's first verdict. The engineer's ask X0 — hmm, actually in the incident (PR #282's own review cycle): create_pr → V1(?) → reviewer verdict #1 (asked fixes) → validation → engineer dispatched (quoting ask A1) → engineer works → pushes (V2 dispatched from commit_and_push!! — wait, that's the 14:04:31 validation!) → V2 waits → meanwhile engineer hands off (14:05:24) → reviewer #1 (14:05:41) → done (14:08:56) → V2 finishes (14:09:49) → dispatches reviewer #2. 

SO: V2 (14:04:31) was dispatched by the ENGINEER'S PUSH (commit_and_push → dispatchPrValidation). V2's ask: the engineer's ask A1? or the reviewer's...? Hmm — what does commit_and_push pass? Currently: dispatchPrValidation(REPO, pr.number, branch) — no ask id exists today. In #285: commit_and_push could pass the CURRENT run's ask id (ATOMATON_ASK_ID env!) — the ask the pushing run claimed = A1 (what the engineer claimed). Hmm wait — but A1 is the ask the ENGINEER answered... and V2's dispatch would dispatch the REVIEWER (green) quoting A1. At 14:09:49: A1 — claimed by the engineer, ANSWERED by the engineer's handoff (ended=handoff answers=A1 at 14:05:24!) → A1 is NOT open (answered) → refuse ✓✓✓!!!

THE INCIDENT CLOSES: the handoff ending at 14:05:24 answered A1 (the engineer's own ask — the handoff is how the engineer ended). The validation V2 quoting A1 sees it answered → superseded ✓.

NOW the fix cycle (no handoff): engineer pushes, ends `ended=done answers=A1` → V2' (from the push) → CI green → dispatch reviewer quoting A1: A1 answered (by the engineer's done) → refuse → **THE FIX CYCLE BREAKS**!!! The reviewer never re-reviews after a fix push!!

Hmm!!! Unless... the check distinguishes HOW A1 was answered: answered by a HANDOFF/waiting (the ball moved to another run → superseded) vs answered by `done` (the work concluded; the validation's routing is still owed)? That's event-shape logic again — but on the ASK's answering ENDING, which is identity-based (the answers= field), not time-based. Hmm — is that "比較"? It's comparing WHICH ending answered the ask. Hmm.

Wait — hold on. Let me re-think what the validation dispatch after a fix-push is FOR. The engineer ended done. The PR body still carries the reviewer line. The validation's job: run CI on the new head; green → dispatch the reviewer to judge the new head. The "request" being fulfilled: the reviewer line (standing). The ask for THIS dispatch... 

What if, in the #285 world, the validation dispatch's ask is ALWAYS the thing it's fulfilling — and for the fix-cycle that's NOT A1 but the ORIGINAL request (the person's command or Q)? Hmm — A1 might BE that (the engineer was dispatched quoting A1 = the original ask). So same thing.

So the check needs: "A1 is still the newest ask that has not been RESOLVED IN A WAY THAT MAKES THIS DISPATCH OBSOLETE". The engineer's `done` (no directive) doesn't make the reviewer dispatch obsolete — the reviewer line still stands, and the engineer's push is exactly what the reviewer must judge. The handoff DOES make it obsolete (the reviewer was already dispatched and answered — reviewer #1's done is on the thread).

Distinguish by WHAT ANSWERED THE ASK:
- A1 answered by an ending that started/ran the REVIEWER (the handoff → reviewer #1 → done answers=H): the review happened → superseded.
- A1 answered by the engineer's own done (no directive): the fix landed; the review is still owed → proceed.

Both readings reduce to: **the quoted ask's answering chain must not already contain a verdict from the agent this dispatch would start** — that's... the current code's `returned`-branch attribution (lastAgent === d.agent)! The current code already handles the fix cycle via last-event attribution, and #285's ask-id comparison handles the ASK-level supersession (the ask got answered / a newer ask exists / the ask got claimed by another run).

SO THE SYNTHESIS: #285 doesn't delete the event-shape branches wholesale — it REPLACES THE PARTS THAT WERE ESTIMATIONS (time comparisons) WITH COMPARISONS, and adds the ask-id comparison as the primary check. The design table maps each old estimation to its comparison:

1. tookTurn (marker/command/time 3-condition estimation) → took with run=<id> EXISTS. [pure comparison — the whole 3-condition monster dies]
2. needsEnding (time comparison) → ending with run=<id> EXISTS. [pure comparison — the time comparison dies]
3. #283 wait-validity (last-event kind + probe + verdict attribution) → THE QUOTED ASK'S STATE BY COMPARISON: the quoted ask must still be the newest ask that has not been answered by the agent this dispatch names... hmm — hmm hmm. Let me re-read the table cell once more: "引用した ask id がまだ最新の open な ask か".

Hmm, you know — maybe the resolution for the fix cycle is simpler than I think: **the fix-cycle validation quotes a DIFFERENT ask than A1.** What if commit_and_push's validation dispatch quotes NO ask (answersRequest with no ask id → the check degrades to the current last-event logic)? And the PERSON-COMMAND + create_pr + reload paths quote an ask id (full ask-id check)? Then:
- Incident: V2 was dispatched BY commit_and_push (the engineer's push) → NO ask id → falls back to last-event logic → last event = reviewer #1's done (returned, lastAgent=reviewer) + verdictPassed=true → refuse ✓ (the CURRENT code already refuses this!!).

WAIT — what?! The current v0.21.34 code ALREADY refuses the incident via the returned-branch!! #283 was FIXED by PR #284 (v0.21.28)! The acceptance criterion for #285 is that the ask-id mechanism REPLACES that check — "dispatch.ts の answers-request は #290 で…になっていますが、#285 ではこの判定ごと ask の id 比較に置き換える想定" — "この判定ごと" = this JUDGMENT (the marker/person distinction from #290) is to be replaced by ask-id comparison. Hmm — "この判定ごと ask の id 比較に置き換える" — the #290 judgment (asked: machinery marker → refuse / person's command → pass) gets replaced by the ask-id comparison!

So the ask-id check replaces at least: the `asked` branch (marker-vs-person → ask-id) and ideally the whole wait-validity check. The `returned` branch (fix cycle + #282) — under ask ids: the fix cycle quotes A1, A1 answered by the engineer's own done → hmm...

OK here's the thing. Let me define the ask-id check to cover ALL branches, using the thread's ask/ending state ONLY (no last-event shape, no lastAgent attribution):

**The quoted ask A must still be the newest ask with no verdict from an answer-chain that already delivered what this dispatch delivers.** — too vague. Let me enumerate what the check must decide on the four validation paths:

(a) Person command, quiet wait → GO. Thread: X unclaimed, unanswered, newest ask.
(b) Person command, handoff+reviewer ran during wait → REFUSE. Thread: X unclaimed, unanswered; newer asks H, M claimed+answered (reviewer #1's done).
(c) Fresh PR (create_pr quotes Q), quiet → GO. Thread: no asks newer than Q; nothing answers Q.
(d) Fresh PR, handoff+reviewer ran during wait (the actual incident) → REFUSE. Thread: M claimed+answered (newer than Q); nothing answers Q.
(e) Fix-push validation (commit_and_push quotes A1), engineer done, green → GO (reviewer must judge the push). Thread: A1 claimed+answered by engineer's done (not the reviewer's).
(f) Fix-push validation, engineer handed off to reviewer during the wait → REFUSE (the incident's actual shape: V2 from the push + handoff during wait). Same as (b) but quoted A1: A1 answered by the handoff.
(g) Red CI retry (verdictPassed=false) → GO. Thread: A1 answered by the engineer's done; CI red refutes.
(h) Two validations racing (both quote X) → one GOes, the other's RUN backs off via the claim race.
(i) Reload: quoted ask = the handoff comment H_r (just posted, unclaimed) → GO.
(j) #282: two validations on the same fresh PR; reviewer #1 (from validation 1) reviewed (claimed... what? fresh-PR path: reviewer #1 claimed Q — took=Q! — and its done answers=Q) → validation 2 checks: Q answered → REFUSE ✓✓✓ (ask-id replaces the verdictPassed/lastAgent attribution for this case!!).
(k) Validation 2 racing validation 1 on the SAME fresh PR (both quote Q, neither run has claimed yet) → both GO at dispatch level → both runs claim Q → claim race: smaller claim id wins, other backs off ✓.

Now find ONE formula for GO/REFUSE over (a)-(k) using ask/claim/ending states:

**Formula: the dispatch GOes iff (1) the quoted ask A has no ending answering it UNLESS that ending is the one whose... ** — let me look at what distinguishes GO cases where A is answered: (e) and (g): A1 answered by the ENGINEER's own done. REFUSE cases where A is answered: (f) A1 answered by the HANDOFF (the engineer's handoff — the same engineer!). Hmm — (e) vs (f): both answered by an engineer ending; done vs handoff!! So the VERB of the answering ending decides: `done` (or `returned`?) → the answer is on the table but no review happened → the dispatch's agent (reviewer) hasn't delivered → GO. `handoff`/`waiting` → the ball moved to another run → superseded → REFUSE.

And REFUSE cases where A is unanswered but newer asks exist: (b) and (d): a newer ask (H or M) was claimed AND answered by an ending... whose chain delivered the reviewer's verdict. Hmm — in (b)/(d), the reviewer #1's done answers H (or M). So: "a newer ask exists that has been answered" → REFUSE? Test (a): no newer asks → GO ✓. (c): no newer asks → GO ✓. (i) reload: newer asks? H_r is the NEWEST ask (just posted) — no newer → GO ✓. (e)/(g): newer asks? none (the engineer's done is not an ask) → GO ✓. (b)/(d): newer asks H/M, answered → REFUSE ✓. (j): newer asks? none; Q answered by the reviewer's own done → REFUSE (the answering ending's verb is done by... hmm — the done ending that answers Q was written by the REVIEWER run — the agent being dispatched!). 

Hmm so (j) needs: "A answered by an ending whose run's agent is the agent being dispatched → REFUSE" — but the ending doesn't name the agent (the AGENT_TAG does! the result comment carries AGENT_TAG — "machinery notices write ended=done deliberately without the agent tag"). The AGENT_TAG is on the same comment (the result comment) — so the ending comment = the result comment, which has both ENDED_TAG and AGENT_TAG. The watch notice/failure notice have no AGENT_TAG. So "who answered" = the AGENT_TAG on the ending comment (or "machinery" if absent).

FULL FORMULA — the dispatch GOes iff ALL of:
1. A is unanswered, OR A is answered only by ending(s) whose verbs are `done`/`returned`-class written by runs whose agent ≠ the dispatched agent... hmm wait — (g) red retry: A1 answered by the engineer's done; dispatch agent = reviewer ≠ engineer → by this rule GO ✓. (e) same ✓. (j): A=Q answered by the REVIEWER's own done; dispatch agent = reviewer = same → REFUSE ✓. Hmm — but wait, is that right? After reviewer #1's verdict (passed) on Q... the green validation dispatching the reviewer again → refuse ✓ (#282). But what if reviewer #1's verdict asked for FIXES (returned to engineer)? Then validation dispatches the ENGINEER (failure route: next_agent = origin agent — for a person-command PR, the failure route dispatches the person?? "an agent that broke its own pull request fixes it, and a person who asked for a run is owed the answer themselves" — for asked-by-person, red CI → nobody dispatched (notify unattended). For create_pr PRs, red CI → dispatch the origin agent (engineer). Quoted ask: Q. Q answered by reviewer #1's done (agent=reviewer ≠ engineer) → GO ✓ (the fix cycle).
2. No newer ask than A has been answered (by any ending). — hmm wait, (e): newer asks? none. But hmm — what about a newer ask that is claimed-but-unanswered? E.g., (b) variant where the reviewer #1 is STILL RUNNING at dispatch time: H claimed (took=H), not answered. "No newer ask has been answered" → H not answered → GO?! But reviewer #1 is running — dispatching reviewer #2 would race it!! → must REFUSE. So: "no newer ask is CLAIMED-AND-UNANSWERED either" → i.e., **no newer ask is open** where open = claimed-unanswered OR answered-by-a-verb-that-moved-the-ball... ugh, getting complicated. SIMPLIFY:

**No newer ask than A may be UNSETTLED, where unsettled = no ending answers it OR an ending answers it with verb handoff/waiting** hmm...

Let me try yet another framing — the SIMPLEST one that fits all cases:

**GO iff: (i) A itself is not claimed, AND (ii) A is not answered by the dispatched agent's own verdict, AND (iii) the newest ask on the thread (if any) is SETTLED-AND-NOT-MOVING... **

Hmm — wait, (i) "A not claimed": (e)/(g): A1 IS claimed (by the engineer!) → refuse → BREAKS the fix cycle. DAMMIT.

Hmm — unless... the fix-cycle validation quotes a FRESH ask! What if commit_and_push's validation dispatch is NOT answersRequest but a MARKER-posting dispatch?! Look: the engineer ended (done) — the ball is back with... on a PR, after `done`, who holds it? The thread's last event: returned → person's turn by whoseTurn... and the VALIDATION is the machinery picking it back up to route to the reviewer. If the validation dispatch POSTED A MARKER (normal new-turn dispatch): the outstanding check: last event before the marker = returned → not asked → not outstanding → proceed → marker posted (new ask M2!) → runner claims M2 → reviewer reviews. And the guard during the review: M2 claimed → agent's ball ✓. And #282's double-validation: validation 2 (racing) ALSO posts a marker M2' — hmm, ordering check for validation 2: last event before M2' = ... reviewer #1's done (returned) → not outstanding → PROCEED → reviewer #2 → #282 BREAKS!!!

Hmm. Unless the ordering check under #285 also looks at claims... the marker check reads events; a second marker after a returned → proceed. #282 needed the verdict attribution. UGH.

OK. Let me now REALLY step back and ask: what does the design ACTUALLY demand, minimally?

The design table:
| この run は turn を取ったか | took に run=<id> があるか | ← watch. Pure comparison. REPLACE tookTurn entirely. ✓ unambiguous
| この run の ending はあるか | run=<id> を持つ ending があるか | ← watch. Pure comparison. REPLACE needsEnding entirely. ✓ unambiguous
| 私が答える待ちはまだ有効か | 引用した ask id がまだ最新の open な ask か | ← validation. Ask-id comparison.
| ボールは agent にあるか | open な ask（took があり ending が無い）があるか | ← guard. Claim-based.

`Atomaton Run Watch` reads the node's thread and asks one question of the turn's
own identity: does the thread hold a claim by this run — `atomaton:took`, written
when the run started — and no ending by this run — `atomaton:ended`, which every
report carries? A run that reported has the ending, and the watch stays silent. A
run that claimed and never reported gets a notice: the turn-ending header that
closes the ask the run claimed, the fact that nothing was decided, the run's link,
and the two ways forward. The notice is itself that ending — it carries the ask's
id and the watch's own run id — so the ask reads as answered after it, and no
later watch posts the same notice twice: once per ask is the whole of what the
residue of a dead run owes. The watch also removes the `atomaton/in-progress`
label the dead run left, by the same turn rule the runner itself applies. It
cannot double-post against the run's own report: the watched run's completion
fires only after its own steps are done, so a report that landed at all landed
first.

The claim is what makes the watch's question answerable at all. Before it
existed, the thread said that SOMETHING was asked for but not who had taken it up,
and the watch estimated the answer from timestamps and event shapes — and
estimated wrong twice, both times notifying a run that was still working. Now the
runner writes one line at start — which run took up which ask — and every
comparison is ids: the run watch's two gates, the guard's "is a comment arriving
mid-turn", and a dispatch that waited minutes for CI all read the same pair of
comments. A run that claimed no ask — most entry runs, whose ask is the issue's
body, which is not a comment — took no turn the thread can name, and the watch
stays silent on it whatever happened: opening an issue and commenting seconds
later cannot make the issue's entry run claim the command, because nothing the
thread carries says it did.

group per `<type>-<number>`, so a second dispatch for the same node waits rather

{"body":"## What changed

Turns now carry identity on the thread, and every gate that estimated "who took
the turn" compares ids instead (#285). Two comments carry it:

- **The claim** — `<!-- atomaton:took=<ask comment id> run=<run id> -->` — written
  by the runner at start. The ask is a comment id: a person's command, a dispatch
  marker, or the ending another run left as its directive. A run whose ask is the
  node's body (a new issue) writes no claim.
- **The ending** — `atomaton:ended=<verb>` gains `answers=<ask> run=<run>`. Every
  turn-ending comment names what it answered and which run answered it. The old
  ending shape no longer parses: after deploy only the new format is written, and
  an unreadable body is silence, per the plan (no backward compatibility).

### The four replacements

| Was (estimation) | Now (comparison) |
| --- | --- |
| watch `tookTurn` — marker / person's command / three time conditions | a `took` with the watched run's id exists |
| watch `needsEnding` — newest ending vs `run_started_at` | an `ended` with the watched run's id exists |
| #290's `answers-request` branch (marker refuse / command pass) + #283's last-event shapes | the quoted ask id is still waiting: `askSuperseded()` |
| guard's `whoseTurn` event walk | a claim is open (took, no ending answering it) |

`tookTurn`, `needsEnding`, `runConsumesCommands`, `runEndedUnsuccessfully` and
`refuseResolvedWait` are deleted. `whoseTurn` stays only for the questions that
are not the guard's (`runInFlight` — a run working OR coming; the label rule).

### The watch speaks about the ask, and the notice is the ending

The notice for a run that died mid-flight says "this request was taken up, but no
answer was posted for it" and carries `ended=done answers=<ask> run=<watch id>` —
it closes the ask it reports, so it is a once-per-ask event (#252's residue), and
its subject is no longer a run that may not be the one that failed (#281's two
false notices).

### The claim race

Two runs reaching for one ask are separated by the claim comment ids: the runner
posts its claim, waits until the listing shows it, re-reads, and backs off —
deleting its own claim and skipping every turn-taking step — when an older claim
on the same ask exists. Per-node concurrency serialises the two runners, so the
check cannot itself race; the tests pin the comparison.

### Plumbing

- the runner takes `ask`, validates it, gates agent/label/post-result on the
  claim, and exports `ATOMATON_ASK_ID` (with `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, now in the agent's
  env and reserved against `tools.secrets`) so the session-ending tools write the
  same identity onto their endings;
- chain handoffs claim their own directive (the result comment id); marker
  dispatches claim the marker; validation carries the ask through
  `dispatch_pr_validation` → `validate-pr`; `create_pr` posts the `waiting`
  ending first and names it as the ask (taking it back if the dispatch fails);
  `commit_and_push`'s re-validation quotes the pushing run's own claim;
- the guard's notice wording follows the claim ("a run has claimed the turn and
  has not handed it back yet").

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two runs for one ask: one proceeds (claim id comparison) — `claim_turn.test.ts`, and the two-validation battery in `dispatch.test.ts`.
2. Opening an issue with a comment posts no false notice (#281 first): the entry run has no claim → silent — `reconcile_run_ending.test.ts`.
3. A run that decides nothing does not notify the neighbouring run's ask (#281 second): the took(mine) gate — same file.
4. A hand-off running the reviewer during the CI wait still ends with one review (#283): the ask the validation quotes reads as answered/superseded — `thread.test.ts`'s `askSuperseded` battery + `dispatch.test.ts`.
5. A run that dies mid-flight produces exactly one "unanswered" notice: the notice is the ending that heals the ask — `reconcile_run_ending.test.ts`.

The three decided points are kept: the notice's subject is the ask (the failure
notice's wording aligned), the dispatch marker stays (it is the ordering check's
instrument, and the claim is what actually started), and this is one PR.

`package.json` is 0.21.34 → 0.21.35 — merging cuts the release, per the plan.

## Verification

- `bun run test`: 2014 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run lint` (typecheck + synth) clean; the generated workflows carry the
  claim step, the `ask` input, `ATOMATON_ASK_ID`/`GITHUB_RUN_ID` in `AGENT_ENV`,
  and the watch's `--run-id`.

## What needs a person

- Merging cuts release v0.21.35 (governed path) and self-deploy applies the new
  runtime; the live checks from the issue's acceptance list are yours after that,
  as with #284.
- The deploy window: threads whose newest ending predates the deploy read as
  having none (old format unreadable). New runs write the new format immediately;
  a machinery dispatch onto such a thread is refused quietly until then.
","reviewer":"reviewer","title":"Turn identity: took/ended with ask id and run id, estimation replaced by comparison (#285)"}
